Scene 03

HOTEL BELMONT

John Doggett

Things that land in your in-box, huh, agent Scully?

Dana Scully

Good morning. I'm sorry I'm late. I didn't get a chance to look at the case file. The traffic's terrible.

John Doggett

Beltway's a nightmare. Takes longer to get crosstown than it does a plane ride from india which is where our victim flew in from last night-- bombay.

Dana Scully

Who are we talking about?

John Doggett

Hugh potocki. Importer/exporter from minneapolis. Laid over in D.C. On his way home when all this blood drains from his body.

Dana Scully

Did the m.e. See it? The body?

John Doggett

Yeah. Tox test ruled out hemorrhagic fever, ebola, anything exotic. Something killed this man but it doesn't seem to be any foreign disease.

Dana Scully

No sign of forced entry?

John Doggett

No. No one was seen coming or going from this room. The maid found the body 20 minutes after a bellman left mr. Potocki here. Whatever happened, happened fast.

Dana Scully

So, basically what you're saying is that nobody knows anything.

John Doggett

But then I guess that's why it's in your in-box. So, what do you think, agent Scully? Haunted hotel room? Alien invaders? Sloppy vampires? There is one small thing. The cops missed it their first time around.

Unidentified speaker

Well, that looks like

Dana Scully

A child's print.

John Doggett

Yeah. That's what it looks like. You know there was a ring of thieves when I was back in new york. They used kids for b&e jobs.

Dana Scully

Mm...

John Doggett

Squeezing in through cracked windows, that kind of thing. But this, this is beyond.

Dana Scully

No. From what I see, agent Doggett, from the way this man died, I doubt it was a kid who did this.

John Doggett

Thanks. I'm not quite ready yet to lose all my faith in humanity.

Dana Scully

But regardless, I'd say it's wise you keep an open mind.

[ kids yelling ]

Scene 04

FAIRMONT ELEMENTARY SCHOOL

Mrs. Holt

The better the economy gets the harder it is to fill these kinds of jobs. And the problem is that people look at it as just a paycheck. They don't realize that as maintenance engineer, you are playing an important part in these kids' lives. And I can't tell you how wonderful it is to find someone as enthusiastic as you are, mr. Burrard. And I understand you can start immediately? That's wonderful.

[ sighs ]

John Doggett

Big fella, isn't he?

Dana Scully

Big is a relative term, agent Doggett. It took three strong men to wheel him in here. He tipped the scale at 402 pounds.

John Doggett

Uh, hugh potocki was a big man, big appetites. Loved big cars, big houses, big business. Divorced twice. He carried two alimonies, one with child support. Never missed a payment. In fact, he seems to have spoiled his wives and kids.

Dana Scully

I'm missing the point.

John Doggett

It seems he loved big women too. Considering the evidence and motives, we can probably rule out his ex-wives as suspects.

Dana Scully

Well, considering what I found here today, I'd say I have to agree. Tissue damage. Massive trauma to the lower intestine and the rectal wall.

John Doggett

Is that from something going in or coming out?

Dana Scully

Well, unfortunately, there's so much damage that it's hard to tell. I took mris, which reveal further shredding throughout the abdomen and, uh, into the stomach area.

John Doggett

India's a major transit point for the golden triangle. This guy flew in and out of india half a dozen times over the past 18 months.

Dana Scully

Are you suggesting that he's a mule? A courier of heroine or opiates? Drug dealer?

John Doggett

Fills a latex balloon with heroin, swallows it. We've all seen this kind of thing before. But what if somebody got to him en route, forcibly extracted the drugs, tearing it from his stomach?

Dana Scully

Well, I'd say, uh, that's a good theory, agent Doggett, not to mention a graphic one, but there would have been traces left of drugs in his system. Nor does it account for the blood loss that this man experienced.

John Doggett

Then we're right back where we started. Nobody knows anything.

Dana Scully

Not exactly. I ran a decay analysis to, uh, determine the time of death. Liver temperature, buildup of gases, extent of rigor-- routine stuff. It's not 100% accurate, but it gives us a range.

John Doggett

What's the range?

Dana Scully

24 to 36 hours.

John Doggett

Well, that's just wrong.

Dana Scully

Well, it would mean that, uh, mr. Potocki here would have died before he left bombay.

John Doggett

No. It would mean that a dead man boarded a plane in india, changed planes in paris, hailed a cab at dulles and then checked into a downtown hotel and tipped the bellman. In my experience, dead men don't tip, agent Scully.

Dana Scully

I told you to keep an open mind.

Scene 06

FBI HEADQUARTERS

John Doggett

Yes. Thank you. Sorry to wake you. Good-bye.

Dana Scully

Bad connection?

John Doggett

Consulate in new delhi. Three weeks ago an american businessman was found dead inside his hotel room. Take a look. A mr. Albert brecht of spokane. The reports have been hard to piece together. The medical records are in hindi. Death certificate's in farsi and the news accounts are in... I don't know-- letters I've never seen before. But I did get you a translation of mr. Brecht's autopsy results. Internal trauma. Tearing in the abdomen. You're the doctor-- it sounds like the same m.o., doesn't it, agent Scully?

Dana Scully

Look at this. Albert brecht's passport was a recent issue and it has his weight at 205 pounds, whereas here, an indian medical examiner has him listed at 238 pounds just two hours after his death.

John Doggett

Well, if there's one thing people lie about, it's their weight.

Dana Scully

Well, that's a pretty big lie. I mean, that's a 33-pound discrepancy.

John Doggett

Well, he was a big man, that's for sure.

Dana Scully

Yeah. As was our D.C. Victim. All the better for accommodation.

John Doggett

Accommodation?

Dana Scully

Well, something has to account for the weight gain, agent Doggett. What if whatever it is that killed these men entered and exited them of its own free will? I mean, something.... Small... With small hands... Living... Inside the victims as a... As a stowaway of sorts.

John Doggett

You know I agree that having an open mind is important to crime solving, but... This theory of yours requires an openness that I'm... I'm just not comfortable with.

Dana Scully

I understand, agent Doggett, and I can't prove it... But I bet that if we had weighed hugh potocki when he first arrived here from bombay that he would have been 33 pounds heavier than his corpse.

John Doggett

It's a theory, agent Scully, but to my mind and... Pretty much the rest of me, it-it... Doesn't work.

Dana Scully

I appreciate your resistance but so far this evidence supports it.

John Doggett

Except one thing... Even if there was something living inside of hugh potocki when he arrived here from bombay... You said that mr. Potocki was already dead.

Oh, absolutely. An-and abilities similar to those you told me about on the phone have been ascribed to what are know as siddhi mystics. The siddhi are a very mysterious and particularly powerful order of fakirs. These siddhi they pass on their secret practices from father to son gaining occult powers with each generation.

John Doggett

What kind of powers?

Totally. Or disguise themselves appearing in front of you as, uh, well, virtually anyone.

John Doggett

I'm sorry, dr. Burks, you're a... You're a professor of what?

Chuck Burks

I run the advanced digital imaging lab at the university of Maryland. And, um, I dabble.

John Doggett

Chuck Burks

Doesn't surprise me.

Dana Scully

What?

Chuck Burks
